system.name: ANPL
system.one_liner: Interactive programming system: the user writes a code sketch with natural-language holes that an LLM implements, then debugs hole by hole from compiler traces.

content.variant_note: a Programming band and a Debugging band repeat the same chain (ANPL Program, ANPL Compiler, Python Program, result grid) on one ARC task, the first ending in a red cross and the second in a green check
content.argues: Users sketch the data flow and leave natural-language holes to an LLM; failed programs are debugged hole by hole via redecomposition, rewording or added I/O.
content.subject: An ARC grid task decomposed into three holes, compiled to Python, found wrong, then repaired by redecomposing one hole, rewording another and giving I/O for a third.

encoding.color_means: tint = phase (blue Programming, peach Debugging); black = system parts (compiler, titles, frames); white box = hole; in Debugging the hole fill shows which edit changed it: pale yellow redecomposed, green reworded, blue given I/O; blue text = hole and function names; red = wrong, green = right
encoding.line_style_means: solid black arrow = data flow; orange dashed vertical line = splits actual traces from expected outputs; orange elbow arrow = failure leads to debugging
encoding.shape_means: white box = hole; tall black box = compiler; black-framed grey box = a program; dark grid thumbnail = task or trace
encoding.marker_means: Hole_n names holes and trace rows; red box on a trace grid = wrong region; red cross and green check = verdict on the program
encoding.emphasis: coloured tabs name the phases; each user edit is a coloured arrow whose colour reappears on the changed hole; the check and cross close each band

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw a human-in-the-loop try-and-repair workflow as two tinted bands that repeat the same chain, end each with a verdict mark, and give every kind of user edit its own colour reused on the element it changes.
lessons.suits: Interactive systems with a try, diagnose, repair loop where a person and a model alternate and several kinds of user edits must be told apart.

evidence: We propose the ANPL (Abstracted Natural Programming Language) system (Figure 1)
Each hole is a stand-alone ANPL program, allowing the user to recursively decompose it further.

summary: ANPL lets a user keep control of LLM code generation by writing a sketch of the data flow and leaving natural-language holes for the model to implement. Figure 1 follows one ARC grid task in two tinted bands. In Programming, the user decomposes the task into an ANPL program with three holes, the ANPL Compiler turns it into Python, and the output grid fails with a red cross. In Debugging, hole traces and expected grids lead the user to redecompose one hole, reword another and give I/O to a third, each edit a coloured arrow; the recompiled program ends with a green check.
summary_zh: ANPL让用户写代码骨架、把子模块以自然语言“洞”交给大模型实现。图1用一道ARC网格题分两条色带：编程阶段拆解并编译但结果错误；调试阶段根据洞的轨迹重新分解、改写描述或补充输入输出，最终通过。
notes: actor-interaction added as third kind for the user and compiler exchange; pre-screen listed stage-pipeline and worked-walkthrough. The red cross and green check, and the coloured action arrows, are drawing devices and are not listed as icons.
